title: The Crow
source_note: NCERT structural and thematic alignment only. All teaching passages, checks, feedback, and assessment situations are original Zidd content.

levels.title: Track the crow's choices
levels.focus: follow what the crow wants, finds, and does
levels.teaching_goal: Read original scenes inspired by The Crow and connect each action to the correct bird or object.

guided_check.teaching_block: Track one action at a time. Wanted tells us a wish; found tells us what appeared later. Do not mix the wish with the result.
guided_check.passage: A black crow wishes for a brighter look. Near the pond, he spots a blue feather.

bridge.teaching_block: Follow the next action. The object comes after the action word fixes; the body part tells where it goes.
bridge.passage: The crow fixes the feather beside his tail and studies his reflection in the water.
bridge.prompt: Where does he put the feather?

masterclass.teaching_block: Several birds may appear. Match laughed, spoke, and listened with the correct doer.
masterclass.passage: Two young crows giggle at the odd decoration. An older crow calmly tells them to stop.
masterclass.prompt: Who tells the young crows to stop?

independent_check.teaching_block: Answer from a fresh scene without choices. Look for the final action, not the first detail.
independent_check.passage: A myna carries three shiny threads to her nest. One thread slips, so she flies down and picks it up.
independent_check.prompt: What does the myna pick up?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer event tracking to getting dressed for a play. Keep who, object, and place connected.
transfer_check.passage: For the school play, Rehan pins a paper star on his cap. His sister ties a ribbon around her wrist.
transfer_check.prompt: What does Rehan put on his cap?

levels.title: Find the poem's caring message
levels.focus: identify how friends value the crow as he is
levels.teaching_goal: Use repeated details about appearance and friendship to state a main idea about self-acceptance.

guided_check.teaching_block: A main idea joins the important details. Here, the friends notice the crow's worry and value him without a costume.
guided_check.passage: Kalu hides his dark wings under bright scraps. His flock says, 'Your strong wings and helpful nature already make you special.'
guided_check.prompt: Which idea best joins both sentences?
options: Friends value Kalu as he is.
accepted_answers: Friends value Kalu as he is.
friends value kalu as he is
his friends accept him as he is

bridge.teaching_block: Separate the message from a small detail. The feather is a detail; accepting oneself is the larger idea.
bridge.passage: Mili thinks her plain brown feathers are dull. Her friend points out how well they hide her among dry branches.
options: A natural feature can have value.
accepted_answers: A natural feature can have value.
what we naturally have can be useful

masterclass.teaching_block: Choose a statement supported by the whole paragraph, not a judgment about one colour.
masterclass.passage: The crows have black feathers, clear calls, and watchful eyes. They work together to warn the flock of danger.
masterclass.prompt: Which sentence states the main idea?
accepted_answers: the crows have many useful qualities

independent_check.teaching_block: State the message in your own words. Mention both the worry and the friend's accepting response.
independent_check.passage: A parrot feels embarrassed because one tail feather is bent. Its friend says the bend does not change its cheerful song or kind nature.
independent_check.prompt: What lesson can the parrot learn?

concept_slots.description: Express acceptance despite the bent feather.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply the message to a new human situation. Show that ability and character matter more than matching others.
transfer_check.passage: At sports day, Ina worries because her shoes are older than her teammates' shoes. She still runs steadily and encourages everyone.
transfer_check.prompt: What helpful message could a teammate give Ina?

concept_slots.description: Reassure Ina that the old shoes do not reduce her worth.
Name a real strength shown in the scene.

levels.title: Explain changing feelings
levels.focus: infer why pride, embarrassment, or relief follows an event
levels.teaching_goal: Link a character's feeling to evidence before and after the flock responds.

guided_check.teaching_block: Feelings have clues in actions and words. Showing off suggests pride; hiding after laughter suggests embarrassment.
guided_check.passage: The crow spreads his borrowed feathers and struts in a circle. He expects every bird to admire him.
guided_check.prompt: How does the crow probably feel?

bridge.teaching_block: Read what changes the feeling. The cause should explain the result, not merely repeat the feeling word.
bridge.passage: Some birds laugh at the crow's uneven feathers. He folds his wings and looks at the ground.
options: He feels embarrassed by the laughter.
accepted_answers: He feels embarrassed by the laughter.

masterclass.teaching_block: Use the final words as evidence. Support from friends can replace shame with relief.
masterclass.passage: His flock says that his black feathers suit him and that they want him beside them. The crow lifts his head again.
masterclass.prompt: What makes the crow feel better?

independent_check.teaching_block: Explain a feeling with one clear cause. Include evidence from the scene rather than guessing.
independent_check.passage: A bulbul sings alone at first. When the other birds join its tune, it hops closer and sings more loudly.
independent_check.prompt: How does the bulbul's feeling change, and why?

concept_slots.description: Name the positive change in feeling.
Connect the change to the other birds joining.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer feeling-and-cause reasoning to teamwork. Name the feeling and the supportive action that causes it.
transfer_check.passage: Ravi's poster has a smudged corner. His group says the drawing is clear and helps him mount it neatly.
transfer_check.prompt: How might Ravi feel after the group helps? Explain.

concept_slots.description: Mention the group's words or help.

levels.title: Use clues for bird words
levels.focus: understand feather, strut, admire, and flock in context
levels.teaching_goal: Infer bird-related words from actions, then use the best word in a new sentence.

guided_check.teaching_block: Use the body-part clue. A feather is one light piece covering a bird; wings are the whole flying parts.
guided_check.passage: One soft feather floats from the pigeon's wing and lands by the bench.
options: one light part covering a bird
accepted_answers: one light part covering a bird
a light part covering a bird

bridge.teaching_block: Notice the proud walking action. Strut does not mean fly or hide.
bridge.passage: The rooster struts across the yard, lifting its feet and holding its head high.

masterclass.teaching_block: A flock is a group, not one bird. Check whether the verb refers to several birds together.
masterclass.passage: At sunset, a flock of parrots crosses the orange sky together.

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the context clue to supply a chapter word. The watchers respect the kite's smooth flight.
independent_check.passage: The children ____ the kite as it circles without flapping.
independent_check.prompt: Write the word that means look at with approval.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use bird vocabulary in a new science-club context. The blank asks for one part, not the entire animal.
transfer_check.passage: The nature guide shows the group a striped ____ found on the path.
transfer_check.prompt: Which chapter word completes the sentence?

levels.title: Tell what each word does
levels.focus: distinguish naming, action, and describing words in bird sentences
levels.teaching_goal: Classify a word by its job in a sentence, not by its position or length.

guided_check.teaching_block: A naming word names a person, place, animal, or thing. In this sentence crow names the animal; black tells what kind.
guided_check.prompt: Which word is a naming word?

bridge.teaching_block: An action word shows what happens. Do not choose the nearby describing word.

masterclass.teaching_block: A describing word tells what kind or how something looks. Feather names the thing; bright describes it.
masterclass.passage: A bright feather lies on the path.

independent_check.teaching_block: Classify the target word in a new sentence. Ask whether it names, acts, or describes.
independent_check.passage: Three sparrows chirp beside the wall.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer word jobs to an art label. Colour words can describe when they tell what kind of object is shown.
transfer_check.passage: The poster shows a silver moon.
transfer_check.prompt: Which word is the describing word?

levels.title: Give a reason about real beauty
levels.focus: answer with a claim and a supporting quality
levels.teaching_goal: Write a brief reason that values actions or character instead of judging appearance.

guided_check.teaching_block: A reason answer has an idea plus evidence. Because should introduce a quality shown in the scene.
guided_check.passage: Nora the crow brings twigs to repair a neighbour's nest.
guided_check.prompt: Which answer explains why Nora is a good friend?
options: Nora is a good friend because she helps repair the nest.
accepted_answers: Nora is a good friend because she helps repair the nest.
nora is a good friend because she helps repair the nest

bridge.teaching_block: Choose evidence about behaviour. A colour or size detail does not prove kindness.
bridge.passage: A crow calls loudly to warn smaller birds about a cat.
bridge.prompt: Which reply gives a supported reason?
options: The crow is caring because it warns the birds.
The crow is dark because it calls.
accepted_answers: The crow is caring because it warns the birds.
the crow is caring because it warns the birds

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass check: state the quality and the action in one deterministic sentence.
masterclass.passage: Bela shares her umbrella with a classmate during rain.
accepted_answers: Bela is thoughtful because she shares her umbrella.
bela is thoughtful because she shares her umbrella

independent_check.teaching_block: Write a natural reason. Name the quality and the action that proves it; many sentence forms are valid.
independent_check.passage: A plain grey pigeon stays beside an injured bird until help arrives.

concept_slots.description: Mention staying with the injured bird.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the idea in a new classroom context. Focus on the child's action, not clothes or looks.
transfer_check.passage: Keshav wears an old sweater. He notices a new student sitting alone and invites her into the game.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain one good quality Keshav shows.

items.passage: A crow finds a red thread and tucks it above one eye.
items.prompt: What does the crow find?

items.passage: A pigeon drops a pale feather. A child places it in a nature tray.
items.prompt: Who places the feather in the tray?

items.passage: The raven lifts a ribbon, but the wind carries it into a bush.
items.prompt: Where does the ribbon land?

items.passage: A hoopoe opens its crest, then folds the feathers flat before flying.
items.prompt: What does the bird do before flying?

items.passage: Titu dislikes his short tail. His flock praises his sharp warning call and quick help.
items.prompt: What is the main message?
options: Titu has valuable qualities as he is.
The flock needs a new call.
accepted_answers: Titu has valuable qualities as he is.
titu has valuable qualities as he is
his qualities matter more than his tail

items.passage: A duck wishes for a swan's neck. Her family reminds her that her broad feet make her a strong swimmer.
items.prompt: Which idea joins the details?
options: Every duck should look like a swan.
accepted_answers: each bird has its own strengths

items.passage: Rupa hides her freckles in a photograph. Her friend says her warm smile is what everyone remembers.
items.prompt: State the message in your own words.

concept_slots.description: Express acceptance of Rupa as she is.

items.passage: A clay cup is not shiny, but it keeps water cool and is used every day.
items.prompt: What larger idea does this example show?

concept_slots.description: Note that shine is not the only value.

items.passage: The peahen steps onto the stage and shows her painting while everyone claps.
items.prompt: How does she probably feel?

items.passage: A sparrow's paper crown falls apart. Her friends help remake it, and she smiles again.
items.prompt: Why does the sparrow smile?
accepted_answers: because her friends remake the crown

items.passage: Nikhil drops his drawing when two children tease it. The teacher displays it and points out its careful details.
items.prompt: How might Nikhil's feeling change? Explain.

concept_slots.description: Connect it to the teacher valuing the drawing.

items.passage: A koel is nervous about singing alone. The class hums softly with her.
items.prompt: Why might the koel become less nervous?

items.passage: A flock of geese flies in a V shape.
items.prompt: Which choice explains flock in this sentence?

items.passage: The child admires the kingfisher's bright blue back and watches it quietly.
items.prompt: Which meaning fits admires?

items.passage: The hen ____ across the yard with her head held high.
items.prompt: Write the word that means walks proudly.

items.passage: One white ____ rests beside the empty nest.
items.prompt: Complete the sentence with a bird word.

items.passage: The quick crow catches a seed.
items.prompt: Which word is an action word?

items.passage: A noisy parrot greets us.
items.prompt: Which word describes the parrot?

items.passage: The eagle circles above the hill.
items.prompt: What job does eagle do?

items.passage: The tiny nest sways.
items.prompt: Write the describing word.

items.passage: A crow leads a thirsty pup to a water bowl.
items.prompt: Which answer explains why the crow is helpful?
options: The crow is helpful because it shows the pup water.
accepted_answers: The crow is helpful because it shows the pup water.
the crow is helpful because it shows the pup water

items.passage: Pallavi includes every classmate in her game.
items.prompt: Choose the supported reason.
options: Pallavi is fair because she includes everyone.
Pallavi is tall because she plays.
accepted_answers: Pallavi is fair because she includes everyone.
pallavi is fair because she includes everyone

items.passage: A brown hen gathers her chicks under her wings during rain.
items.prompt: Explain one admirable quality the hen shows.

items.passage: Mita's bag is faded. She lends her new classmate a notebook and shows him the classroom.
items.prompt: What makes Mita a good classmate?
